card.what: Forged stainless bow (lyre) shackle, 5 mm pin with a flat key head: the shackle for loads that pull at an angle
card.boats: J/22 jib tack at the stemhead, halyard shackles on the sail heads, blocks on padeyes; the Sunfish's halyard to the upper spar
card.distance: arm's reach on the foredeck and at the mast; the camera passes close when rigging
card.before: none: the kit had no bow shackle; the old ShackleD (a bent tube and a loose pin) stood in for every shackle

references.use: outline and proportions (square-on catalogue photo of a forged 5 mm-class bow shackle with a key-head pin)
references.url: Bean's hardware reference sheet (project upload, Nov 8 2026), top row 'Bow Shackle'
references.licence: for measuring and look only; never committed or shared

references.use: a bow shackle in the hand (lifting-style, rounder): body and pin read only

references.note: 5 mm forged stainless self-locking bow shackle: L 36 mm overall, A 23 mm inside length, B 10 mm opening, M 25 mm across the bow; matching inch figures at mealeymarine.com (A 29/32, B 25/64, M 63/64 in). Other 5 mm bows: opening 9-10 mm, inside length 17.5-23 mm (S3i essential range, GS Products, Hunt Office)

sizes.name: Width with the key head
sizes.source: square-on photo scaled to the catalogue's 36 mm (220 x 284 px): bow 25 mm across plus the key head

features.text: Round crown swelling wider than the opening (the lyre shape), legs pinching in to the ears
Round 5 mm forged body, one piece with its ears (no seams where the legs meet the ears)
Two flat round ears at the pin, growing out of the legs
5 mm pin right through both ears
Flat key head on one end of the pin, with a hole for seizing wire
Collar between the key head and the ear
Rounded pin end just proud of the far ear
10 mm opening between the ears (takes a 10 mm line's thimble or a block's eye)

budget.note: hero is a Nanite part; a shackle is small, so the build aims at about 13k
